chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"The Takbir in Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha is twelve Takbirat: he says one Takbir in the first [rak'ah], then recites, then says five Takbirat after the recitation, and the seventh is for bowing; then he stands in the second [rak'ah], recites, then says four Takbirat, and the fifth is for bowing."
And he said: "It is appropriate for the Imam to wear a silk garment (Hullah) and wear a turban, whether it is of wool or of silk."

key_terms.اَلْفِطْرِ: Eid al-Fitr (Festival of Breaking the Fast)
key_terms.حُلَّةٌ: A fine silk garment or cloak

ai.seo_question: How many Takbirat are performed in each rak'ah of the Eid prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides a precise juristic breakdown of the Eid prayer structure, specifying twelve Takbirs distributed across the two rak'ahs, a detail crucial for distinguishing Shia ritual practice from other schools. It further highlights the Sunnah of the Imam wearing a 'hullah' (typically silk for men) and a turban, reflecting the tradition of dignified appearance during communal celebrations. This emphasis on both ritual precision and aesthetic reverence underscores the holistic nature of Eid worship in Shia fiqh.
